Nepal earthquake: Experts knew it was coming

That's kind of a misleading title. Sure they knew there would be some large quake in the future because they're overdue for one. But saying they knew it was coming vs knew that it was bound to happen is a big difference Symantecly.

Yes, earthquake prediction can be a chancy affair, and it can't be done 'by the clock'. The conference that was held in Kathmandu 1 week before the event, however, didn't just deal with bare geological facts. It also dealt with the risks involved in Nepal's 'infrastructure' (including non-government construction) and disaster preparedness. There are numerous examples across the world where governments won't listen to sensible advise from geologists. When the inevitable happens they often try to blame the geologists who cannot give any exact timetable, The legalities that swirled around the 2012 earthquake in Aquila Italy was a prime example of this.
